cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 29,133 male smokers 50 to 69 years of age from southwestern Finland were randomly assigned to one of four regimens: alpha-tocopherol (50 mg per day) alone, beta carotene (20 mg per day) alone, both alpha-tocopherol and beta carotene, or placebo.
reason: The trial reports incident prostate cancer as a secondary cancer outcome but does not analyze aggressive, high-grade, advanced, metastatic, or lethal prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Fewer cases of prostate cancer were diagnosed among those who received alpha-tocopherol than among those who did not.
estimate_classifications.reason: This explicitly describes prostate cancer diagnoses according to alpha-tocopherol assignment, without an aggressive-disease restriction.

The abstract describes beta-carotene assignment and broadly states that beta carotene had little or no effect on cancers other than lung cancer, but it does not explicitly identify a beta-carotene estimate for prostate cancer. The supplied existing evidence also does not establish a prostate cancer endpoint for this row.
